caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 309 of 2005.
lawyer:
SN Goswami, Advocate, instructed by Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record---For the Petitioners. 
Not represented---Respondents.
parties:
Dr SM Yunus Ali and  anr ------ Petitioners
vs
Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Tafazzul Islam J: This petition for leave to appeal arises out of the judgment and order dated 27-2-2005 of the High Court Division passed in Writ Petition No. 1055 of 2005 summarily rejecting the application filed by the defendant petitioner challenging the judgment and decree dated 25-7-2004 as well as the subsequent order dated 4-1-2005 of the Second Court of the Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Bagerhat, passed in Artha Rin Case No. 14 of 2003 rejecting the application dated 14-8-2004 filed by the defendant petitioner under section 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 3. The plaintiff/respondent No. 2 examined one witness as PW 1 and the defendant/ petitioner also examined one witness as DW 1 and then next date of the case was fixed on 10-7-2004 for delivery of judgment and subsequently the said date was shifted to 25-7-2004 and in the meantime, on 21-7-2004, the petitioner filed an application under Order XXVI, rule 11, CPC for appointment of an Advocate Commissioner to examine the accounts of the petitioner maintained with the plaintiff but the learned Joint District Judge, rejecting the said prayer, took up the suit for hearing on 25-7-2004, the date fixed, and by judgment and decree dated 25-7-2004 decreed the suit for Taka 47,89,412. Then, on 14-8-2004, the plaintiff filed an application under section 152 CPC praying for correction of the above judgment and decree dated 25-7-2004 and, after hearing, the learned Joint District Judge by order dated 17-8-2004 amended the judgment and decree to the effect that- 

 Thereafter, the petitioner, on 2-11-2004, filed an application under section 152, CPC praying for setting aside the above judgment and decree dated 25-7-2004 on the ground that without considering Exhibit Ga the above judgment and decree dated 25-7-2004 was passed and the learned Joint District Judge, after hearing, by judgment and order dated 4-1-2005 rejected the above application and being aggrieved the petitioner moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and the High Court Division summarily rejected the same. 

 4. The learned Counsel for the defendant No.2/petitioner submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in not considering that in Exhibit Ga the value of the mortgaged property was shown at Taka 33,50,000 whereas the loan amount was to the tune of Taka 20,90,804 and that the scope of section 152, CP was enough to cover such a case of non-consideration of the above Exhibit 'Ga', a vital document, and it is the duty of the Court to see the judgment and decree dated 25-7-2004 be set aside when there is no doubt that the same was passed by mistake and the High Court Division on misinterpretation of section 152, CPC rejected the above application summarily holding that the prayer as made by the petitioner in the application dated 2-11-2004 under section 152, CPC can only be made in the form of appeal and that the alleged mistake, being not a mistake on the part of the Court may be a case of non-consideration of Exhibit 'Ga' and the High Court Division erred in law in overlooking that there being an accidental omission, appeal/review was not the only remedy open to the petitioner and that section 152, CPC was wide enough to cover such a case of accidental omission or an error. 

 5. As it appears the High Court Division rejected the revisional application summarily holding that the prayer as made in the application dated 2-11-2004 for setting aside the judgment and decree dated 25-7-2004 being not covered by section 152, CPC, the Court cannot allow such relief and further, the Court became functus officio after passing of the judgment and decree and the learned Joint District Judge having passed its judgment and decree dated 25-7-2004 on the basis of the sanction letter there was no accidental or arithmetical mistake and the relief as sought in the application dated 2-11-2004 under section 152, CPC could only be made in the form of an appeal as there was no mistake on the part of the Court and rather the same may be regarded as a case of non-consideration of Exhibit Ga.
